questions.question: According to SBI’s January 2025 report, what was India’s rural poverty rate in FY24?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**4.86%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• According to the **SBI Research** report titled "Poverty Reduction in India: A Perspective" released in **January 2025**, India has witnessed a significant decline in its poverty rates.
 
• The report highlights that India’s **rural poverty rate** for **FY24** (Financial Year 2023-24) dropped to **4.86%**. This represents a substantial improvement in the living standards of the rural population. ***Hence, the correct option is 4.86%.***
 
• The **urban poverty rate** for the same period (**FY24**) was recorded at a much lower level of **1.57%**, indicating that urban centers have also seen drastic reductions in extreme deprivation.
 
• Combining these figures, the **national average poverty rate** (Headcount Ratio) for India in **FY24** stands at **3.86%**.
 
• This data is primarily based on the **Household Consumption Expenditure Survey (HCES) 2022-23**, which was extrapolated and analyzed to provide insights into the **FY24** scenario.

questions.question: Who won the Best Director award at the 71st National Film Awards, held in 2025 (honoring 2023 films)?

options.text: Karan Johar — Rocky Aur Rani Kii Prem Kahaani

questions.solution:
p>The correct answer is __**Sudipto Sen — The Kerala Story**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **71st National Film Awards**, which were organized in **2025**, specifically aimed to honor and recognize cinematic excellence for films released or certified during the **year 2023**.
 
• **Sudipto Sen** was adjudged the winner of the **Best Director** award for his work on the film **The Kerala Story**. This award is one of the highest individual honors presented in the Indian film industry.
 
• The film **The Kerala Story** gained national attention for its depiction of sensitive socio-political issues, and the directorial award highlights the technical and narrative execution led by **Sudipto Sen**.
 
• The ceremony continued the tradition of the **National Film Awards** in providing a platform where mainstream cinema and regional art films are evaluated on a common standard of excellence.
 
• The selection for this category was made by a **National Jury** comprising distinguished filmmakers and artists from across the country, ensuring a rigorous evaluation of directorial craft including **storytelling**, **character development**, and **technical proficiency**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **National Film Awards Overview:**
 
 
• Established in **1954**, the **National Film Awards** are the most prestigious film awards in **India**. They are considered equivalent to the state honors given to individual excellence in the arts.
 
• The awards are administered by the **Directorate of Film Festivals**, which functions under the **Ministry of Information and Broadcasting** of the **Government of India**.
 
• Unlike commercial film awards (such as Filmfare or IIFA), these awards are focused on the **aesthetic**, **technical**, and **social** relevance of the films rather than their box office performance.
 
 
 
• **Award Categories:**
 
 
• The awards are divided into several sections, primarily **Feature Films**, **Non-Feature Films**, and **Best Writing on Cinema**.
 
• The **Best Director** award falls under the **Feature Film** section and is traditionally rewarded with the **Swarna Kamal** (Golden Lotus) trophy and a cash prize.
 
• Other major categories include **Best Feature Film**, **Best Actor**, and **Best Actress**, which recognize the comprehensive effort of the cast and crew.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Eligibility Criteria:**
 
 
• To be eligible for the **71st National Film Awards**, a film must have been certified by the **Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC)** between **January 1, 2023, and December 31, 2023**.
 
• The awards are open to films made in any **Indian language**, promoting **linguistic diversity** and **regional cinema** on a national stage.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Director's Role:**
 
 
• The **Best Director** honor recognizes the person responsible for the creative vision and the overall management of the film's production, from **screenplay execution** to **cinematographic style**.
 
• Winners of this award are often cited for their ability to balance **artistic integrity** with **audience engagement**, contributing significantly to the cultural fabric of **Indian Cinema**.

questions.question: Which male athlete set new world indoor records in both the 1500 m (3:29.63 en route) and the mile (3:45.14) on 13 Feb 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jakob Ingebrigtsen**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jakob Ingebrigtsen**, the prolific **Norwegian** middle-distance runner, achieved a historic double world record on **February 13, 2025**.
 
• During the **Meeting Hauts-de-France Pas-de-Calais** held in **Liévin**, **France**, he shattered two world indoor records in a single race.
 
• He clocked a sensational **3:45.14** for the **mile**, significantly lowering the previous **world indoor record** of **3:47.01** held by **Yomif Kejelcha** since **2019**.
 
• As he completed the **1500-meter** portion of the race, he was timed at **3:29.63** (en route), which also established a new **world indoor record** for that distance, breaking his own previous mark of **3:30.60**.
 
• This performance cemented his status as one of the greatest distance athletes in history, holding multiple indoor and outdoor records simultaneously.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Jakob Ingebrigtsen Profile**: Born on **September 19, 2000**, in **Sandnes**, **Norway**, he is an **Olympic Gold Medalist** in the **1500m** (**Tokyo 2020**) and **5000m** (**Paris 2024**). He has been coached primarily by his family and is known for his high-volume training threshold method.
 
• **World Indoor Records**: Indoor records are set on **200-meter** banked tracks, which are generally slower than the standard **400-meter** outdoor tracks. Ingebrigtsen's mile time of **3:45.14** is remarkably close to the outdoor world record of **3:43.13** set by **Hicham El Guerrouj** in **1999**.
 
• **Meeting Hauts-de-France Pas-de-Calais**: This meeting is part of the **World Athletics Indoor Tour Gold** series. The track in **Liévin** is legendary for middle-distance running, having hosted numerous world records in the **1500m**, **2000m**, and **3000m**.
 
• **Competing Athletes**: Other athletes mentioned in the options, such as **Yared Nuguse** (**USA**) and **Cole Hocker** (**USA**), are his primary rivals. **Nuguse** previously held the **North American indoor mile record**, and **Hocker** is the **Paris 2024 Olympic 1500m champion**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **En Route Timing**: In **World Athletics** sanctioned events, an athlete can set a world record for a shorter distance (like the **1500m**) during a longer race (like the **mile**), provided the timing is recorded electronically at the specific mark.
 
• **Wavelight Technology**: The race in **Liévin** utilized **Wavelight technology**, a visual pacing system using **LED lights** along the inside rail of the track, which helped **Ingebrigtsen** maintain the precise **world-record pace** required to beat **Kejelcha's** **2019** time.
 
• **Impact on Athletics**: This performance marked the first time an athlete had broken the **3:30** barrier for **1500m** and the **3:46** barrier for the **mile** indoors, showcasing the rapid advancement in middle-distance running speeds.

questions.question: Who among the following headed the three-member committee formed in August 2025 to assess the Dharali disaster damage in Uttarakhand?

options.text: CEO of Indian Civil Aviation Authority
Home Minister of India, Amit Shah
Uttarakhand Chief Minister, Pushkar Singh Dhami

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Uttarakhand Revenue Secretary, Surendra Pandey**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **August 2025**, the **Uttarakhand Government** constituted a specialized **three-member committee** to conduct a thorough assessment of the damages resulting from the **Dharali disaster** in the **Uttarkashi district**.
 
• The committee was led by the **Uttarakhand Revenue Secretary**, **Surendra Pandey**, who was tasked with overseeing the technical and administrative evaluation of the affected regions.
 
• The primary objective of this committee was to quantify the loss of **public infrastructure**, **private property**, and **agricultural land** to ensure the timely disbursement of compensation and relief funds.
 
• The formation of this high-level committee followed reports of significant cloudburst-induced damage in the **Bhagirathi valley**, specifically affecting the **Dharali** and **Harsil** sectors.
 
• The committee's findings were designated to serve as the basis for the state's request for additional financial assistance from the **National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF)**.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Uttarakhand Revenue Secretary, Surendra Pandey__.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Geography of Dharali:**
 
 
• **Dharali** is a picturesque village located at an altitude of approximately **2,680 meters** in the **Uttarkashi district** of **Uttarakhand**.
 
• It is situated on the banks of the **Bhagirathi River** (a headstream of the Ganges) and is renowned for its **apple orchards** and proximity to the **Gangotri National Park**.
 
 
 
• **Role of the Revenue Secretary:**
 
 
• In the administrative hierarchy of **Uttarakhand**, the **Revenue Secretary** serves as a pivotal figure in **disaster management**, as the department is responsible for land records and the assessment of natural calamity losses.
 
• The secretary coordinates with the **District Magistrates (DM)** to implement the **State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF)** guidelines and ensure administrative transparency during crisis recovery.
 
 
 
• **Disaster Management Framework:**
 
 
• Assessment committees typically operate under the **Disaster Management Act, 2005**, which provides the legal framework for the preparation, mitigation, and response to disasters in **India**.
 
• In **Uttarakhand**, the **State Disaster Management Authority (SDMA)**, chaired by the **Chief Minister**, works in tandem with the **Revenue Department** to handle such crises.
 
 
 
• **Vulnerability of the Region:**
 
 
• The **Uttarkashi region** is highly susceptible to **flash floods**, **cloudbursts**, and **landslides** due to its fragile Himalayan topography and high-intensity rainfall during the monsoon months.
 
• The **2025 disaster** in **Dharali** underscored the need for continuous monitoring of glacial streams and the implementation of **Early Warning Systems (EWS)** along the **Char Dham** pilgrimage route.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **three-member committee** included technical experts from the **Public Works Department (PWD)** and the **Irrigation Department** to evaluate structural integrity.
 
• **Surendra Pandey**, an **IAS officer**, emphasized the use of **drone surveys** and **satellite imagery** for precise mapping of the disaster-affected zones in **August 2025**.
 
• The **Dharali** area is a significant stop for pilgrims traveling to **Gangotri**, making its rapid restoration a priority for the state's **tourism and pilgrimage** economy.
</ul

questions.question: In which of the following districts of Madhya Pradesh is Kuno National Park located?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sheopur**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kuno National Park** is located in the **Sheopur** and **Morena** districts of **Madhya Pradesh** in **India**.
 
• It was initially established as a **Wildlife Sanctuary** in the year **1981** with an area of about **344.68 sq. km**.
 
• The government of **Madhya Pradesh** upgraded the status of the sanctuary to a **National Park** in **December 2018**, increasing its area to **748.76 sq. km**.
 
• This park is famous for being the site of **Project Cheetah**, the world's first intercontinental large wild carnivore translocation project.
 
• In **September 2022**, **eight African Cheetahs** were brought from **Namibia** and released into the park by **Prime Minister Narendra Modi**.
 
• The park is part of the **Khathiar-Gir dry deciduous forests** ecoregion and is nestled in the **Vindhyan Hills**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Geography and Flora**:
 
 
• The park is named after the **Kuno River**, which flows through the center of the park from **South to North**.
 
• The forest type is primarily **Northern Tropical Dry Deciduous Forest**, dominated by trees like **Kardhai** (Anogeissus pendula), **Khair** (Acacia catechu), and **Salai** (Boswellia serrata).
 
• The terrain is a mix of sprawling **grasslands** and dense woodlands, which provides an ideal habitat for herbivores and predators alike.
 
 
 
• **Fauna**:
 
 
• Apart from cheetahs, the park is home to a variety of animals including **Leopards**, **Chital** (spotted deer), **Sambar**, **Nilgai**, **Chinkara**, and **Wild Boar**.
 
• It was originally identified as a secondary home for the **Asiatic Lion** to prevent the species from extinction due to potential epidemics in the **Gir National Park**.
 
 
 
• **Madhya Pradesh Wildlife**:
 
 
• **Madhya Pradesh** is known as the **"Tiger State of India"** because it consistently records the highest tiger population in the **All India Tiger Estimation** reports.
 
• The state hosts several other famous national parks such as **Kanha**, **Bandhavgarh**, **Pench**, **Satpura**, and **Panna**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Project Cheetah Milestones**:
 
 
• Following the first batch from **Namibia**, a second batch of **12 cheetahs** was introduced from **South Africa** in **February 2023**.
 
• The reintroduction marks the return of the cheetah to **India** after it was declared **extinct** in the country in **1952**.
 
 
 
• **District Context**:
 
 
• **Sheopur** district, where the park is primarily situated, is located in the **Chambal Division** of **Madhya Pradesh**.
 
• The **Chambal River** flows nearby, forming the boundary between **Madhya Pradesh** and **Rajasthan**.
 
• The local tribal community, the **Sahariya** tribe, lived within the forest area before being relocated during the expansion of the sanctuary.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following days marks the anniversary of the entry into force of the United Nations Charter (the day the UN was formally established)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**24 October**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **United Nations Day** is celebrated on **24 October** every year to mark the anniversary of the entry into force of the **UN Charter** in **1945**.
 
• With the ratification of this founding document by the majority of its signatories, including the **five permanent members** of the **Security Council**, the **United Nations** officially came into being.
 
• The **United Nations General Assembly** declared this day in **1947**, and it has been celebrated since **1948** to make known to the people of the world the aims and achievements of the **United Nations**.
 
• In **1971**, the **General Assembly** adopted a resolution (**Resolution 2782**) recommending that **United Nations Day** should be a public holiday in all **Member States**.
 
• The **UN Charter** was signed on **26 June 1945** in **San Francisco**, at the conclusion of the United Nations Conference on International Organization, and came into force on **24 October 1945**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **10 December (Human Rights Day)**:
 
 
• This day commemorates the **United Nations General Assembly's** adoption and proclamation of the **Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR)** on **10 December 1948**.
 
• The **UDHR** is a milestone document that set out, for the first time, fundamental human rights to be universally protected.
 
 
 
• **7 April (World Health Day)**:
 
 
• Observed every year on **7 April**, this date marks the anniversary of the founding of the **World Health Organization (WHO)** in **1948**.
 
• Each year, a specific health theme is chosen to highlight a priority area of concern for the **WHO**, such as mental health, maternal care, or climate change.
 
 
 
• **5 June (World Environment Day)**:
 
 
• This is the **United Nations'** principal vehicle for encouraging awareness and action for the protection of the environment.
 
• It was established by the **UN General Assembly** in **1972** on the first day of the **Stockholm Conference on the Human Environment** and was first celebrated in **1973**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The name **"United Nations"** was devised by **United States President Franklin D. Roosevelt** and was first used in the **Declaration by United Nations** of **1 January 1942**.
 
• The **United Nations** is headquartered in **New York City**, but it also has significant offices in **Geneva**, **Nairobi**, and **Vienna**.
 
• The **UN** currently consists of **193 Member States** and **2 Observer States** (Holy See and Palestine).
 
• The main organs of the **UN** are the **General Assembly**, the **Security Council**, the **Economic and Social Council**, the **Trusteeship Council**, the **International Court of Justice**, and the **UN Secretariat**.
 
• The **International Court of Justice (ICJ)** is the only principal organ not located in **New York**; it is located in **The Hague**, **Netherlands**.
</ul

questions.question: In June 2025, which Indian state withdrew the three-language policy for schools and formed a committee headed by educationist Narendra Jadhav to suggest the way forward?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Maharashtra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **June 2025**, the state government of **Maharashtra** officially announced the withdrawal of the existing **three-language policy** in schools to pave the way for a more flexible and modernized linguistic curriculum.
 
• To determine the new educational framework, the state formed a specialized committee led by the prominent educationist and economist **Narendra Jadhav**.
 
• The **Narendra Jadhav committee** is tasked with evaluating the impact of the previous policy and suggesting a way forward that aligns with the evolving needs of students in a globalized environment while preserving the importance of the **regional language**.
 
• This move follows growing discussions regarding the administrative and academic burden on students and the need to emphasize **Marathi** as the primary medium of instruction and cultural identity in the state.
 
• The committee includes various experts from the field of education who will submit a comprehensive report detailing the language requirements for primary and secondary education levels in **Maharashtra**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Three-Language Formula:**
 
 
• The formula was first formulated by the **Union Ministry of Education** in **1968** as part of the **National Policy on Education**.
 
• It typically involves the study of **Hindi**, **English**, and a **regional language** in non-Hindi speaking states, and Hindi, English, and a modern Indian language in Hindi-speaking states.
 
• The primary objective of this formula was to promote national integration and multilingualism among Indian students.
 
 
 
• **Narendra Jadhav:**
 
 
• **Narendra Jadhav** is a renowned Indian **economist**, **educationist**, and **author** who has served as a member of the **Planning Commission of India**.
 
• He also served as a **nominated member of the Rajya Sabha** from **2016 to 2022** and has held the position of **Vice-Chancellor** of **Savitribai Phule Pune University**.
 
• His expertise is frequently sought by both **State and Central Governments** for drafting policies related to **social justice** and **educational reforms**.
 
 
 
• **Linguistic Policy in Maharashtra:**
 
 
• **Marathi** was made a compulsory subject in all schools in **Maharashtra**, regardless of the board affiliation (SSC, CBSE, ICSE, or IB), through the **Maharashtra Compulsory Teaching and Learning of Marathi Language Act, 2020**.
 
• The withdrawal of the three-language policy in **2025** indicates a shift toward prioritizing **regional proficiency** and reducing the curriculum load in alignment with **state-specific priorities**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 Connection:**
 
 
• The **NEP 2020** provides states with the flexibility to choose the three languages they wish to teach, provided at least two of the three languages are **native to India**.
 
• The **Maharashtra** government's decision to review its policy through the **Narendra Jadhav committee** is seen as a localized implementation strategy of the broader **NEP guidelines**.
 
 
 
• **Committee Objectives:**
 
 
• The committee will focus on the **cognitive development** of children through **mother-tongue-based** instruction in the early years.
 
• It will also look into the **implementation challenges** faced by schools in rural versus urban areas regarding language faculty and resources.
 
 
 
• **Date and Context:**
 
 
• The decision made in **June 2025** reflects a significant turning point in the **educational history of Maharashtra**, aiming to balance the **Marathi language's** heritage with **English's** global utility.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: Who is the author of the memoir Mother Mary Comes to Me, launched in September 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Arundhati Roy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The memoir titled **Mother Mary Comes to Me** is authored by the acclaimed writer **Arundhati Roy**, marking her first foray into full-length memoir writing.
 
• The book is scheduled for a simultaneous global launch in **September 2025**. It will be published by **Hamish Hamilton** in **India** and the **United Kingdom**, and by **Scribner** in the **United States**.
 
• The narrative centers on the author's complex and "unnatural" relationship with her mother, **Mary Roy**, who was a famous educator and women's rights activist in **Kerala**. ***Hence, the statement regarding the author is correct.***
 
• The memoir explores **Arundhati Roy**’s childhood in **Kerala**, her life as a young architecture student, and her journey toward becoming a world-renowned literary figure.
 
• It reflects on how the death of her mother in **September 2022** influenced her to finally write about their shared history and the impact **Mary Roy** had on her life and politics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Arundhati Roy:**

• Her second novel, **The Ministry of Utmost Happiness**, was published in **2017**, twenty years after her first, and was longlisted for the **Man Booker Prize**.
 
• In addition to fiction, she has published several non-fiction works such as **The Algebra of Infinite Justice** and **Azadi: Freedom. Fascism. Fiction.**, focusing on **human rights** and **environmentalism**.
 
 
 
• **Mary Roy:**
 
 
• She was a pioneering **educator** who founded **Pallikoodam** school in **Kottayam**.
 
• She is famously known for winning a landmark **Supreme Court** case in **1986** that ensured equal inheritance rights for **Syrian Christian women** in **Kerala**.

• The memoir is expected to provide deep insights into the semi-autobiographical elements found in **The God of Small Things**, particularly the social landscape of **Ayemenem**.

questions.question: As stated by French President Emmanuel Macron on 9 June 2025, how many countries had ratified the High Seas Treaty by that date?
questions.solution:
p>The correct answer is __**49**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• French President **Emmanuel Macron** announced on **9 June 2025**, during the lead-up to the **UN Ocean Conference** in **Nice**, that **49 countries** had ratified the **High Seas Treaty**.

• The treaty, formally known as the **BBNJ Treaty** (Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction), requires **60 ratifications** to officially enter into force.

• This announcement was a significant milestone in the global effort to protect international waters, which cover nearly **two-thirds** of the global ocean surface. ***Hence, the correct answer is 49.***

• The **High Seas Treaty** was adopted by the **United Nations** on **19 June 2023**, following nearly two decades of negotiations to establish a legal framework for the conservation of marine life in international waters.

• The treaty aims to establish **Marine Protected Areas (MPAs)** in the high seas, which are areas beyond the **Exclusive Economic Zones (EEZ)** of individual nations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **The BBNJ Agreement:**

• It is an international agreement under the **United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS)**.

• It focuses on four main pillars: **Marine Genetic Resources (MGRs)**, Area-based management tools including **Marine Protected Areas**, **Environmental Impact Assessments (EIAs)**, and Capacity building and the transfer of marine technology.

• The treaty is vital for achieving the **"30x30" goal**, a target set under the **Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework** to protect **30%** of the world’s land and oceans by the **year 2030**.

• **Ratification Process:**

• For an international treaty to become legally binding, a country must first **sign** it and then **ratify** it through its domestic legislative process.

• The **60-country threshold** is the designated number required to trigger the treaty's activation **120 days** after the 60th instrument of ratification is deposited.

• President **Emmanuel Macron** has been a vocal advocate for the treaty, launching the **High Ambition Coalition** on BBNJ at the **One Ocean Summit** in **Brest, France**, in **February 2022**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **The High Seas:**

• These are areas of the ocean that do not belong to any state's jurisdiction. They represent **95%** of the Earth's habitat by volume but are among the least protected regions on the planet.

• Before this treaty, only about **1%** of the high seas were under any form of management or protection.

• The **2025 UN Ocean Conference** in **Nice, France**, co-hosted by **France** and **Costa Rica**, served as a major platform for accelerating the ratification count toward the **60-nation** target.

• **Marine Genetic Resources:** One of the most debated aspects of the treaty involves the equitable sharing of benefits derived from **genetic material** of marine plants and animals found in the deep sea.

questions.question: The Environment Audit Rules, 2025, are aligned with which national reform agenda in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ease of Doing Business**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Environment (Audit) Rules, 2025**, have been formulated by the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)** to streamline the process of environmental compliance for industries in **India**.
 
• These rules are a significant step toward the national reform agenda of **Ease of Doing Business**, as they aim to reduce the regulatory burden on project proponents by simplifying reporting mechanisms.
 
• The primary objective is to replace the traditional "command and control" inspection regime with a more transparent, **self-regulatory**, and **third-party verification** system.
 
• Under these rules, industries are required to conduct regular audits to ensure they are meeting the standards set during their **Environmental Clearance (EC)** process.
 
• The alignment with **Ease of Doing Business** is evident as the rules promote **predictability**, **transparency**, and **efficiency** in environmental governance, which are critical for attracting **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Environment (Protection) Act, 1986**:
 
 
• The **Environment (Audit) Rules, 2025**, are framed under the powers conferred by the **Environment (Protection) Act, 1986**, which was enacted following the **Bhopal Gas Tragedy** of **1984**.
 
• This umbrella legislation provides the **Central Government** with the authority to protect and improve environmental quality and control pollution.
 
 
 
• **Accreditation of Auditors**:
 
 
• The rules mandate that environmental audits must be carried out by **accredited environmental auditors** or agencies recognized by the **Quality Council of India (QCI)** or the **National Accreditation Board for Education and Training (NABET)**.
 
• This ensures that the data provided to the **government** is accurate, professional, and scientifically sound.
 
 
 
• **PARIVESH Portal**:
 
 
• The **Environment Audit** reports are integrated into the **PARIVESH** (Pro-Active and Responsive facilitation by Interactive, Virtuous and Environmental Single-window Hub) portal.
 
• This **digital India** initiative serves as a **single-window** system for all environmental, forest, wildlife, and CRZ clearances, further enhancing the **Ease of Doing Business**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Categorization and Frequency**:
 
 
• Industries are often categorized into **Red**, **Orange**, and **Green** categories based on their **Pollution Index (PI)**. The **2025 Rules** specify different audit frequencies based on these categories to optimize resources.
 
• High-pollution (**Red**) industries are subject to more frequent and rigorous environmental audits compared to less polluting ones.
 
 
 
• **Compliance and Penalties**:
 
 
• The rules emphasize **compliance** with the conditions stipulated in the **Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA)**.
 
• Non-compliance or submission of fraudulent audit reports can lead to heavy **penalties**, **cancellation of clearances**, or legal action under **Section 15** of the **Environment (Protection) Act**, which includes **imprisonment** for up to **5 years** or a fine up to **1 lakh rupees**, or both.
 
 
 
• **Sustainable Development Goals (SDG)**:
 
 
• While focusing on **Ease of Doing Business**, the rules also align with **India's** commitment to **Sustainable Development Goals**, specifically **SDG 12** (Responsible Consumption and Production) and **SDG 13** (Climate Action).
 
 
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct Act, set to be replaced by the Indian Ports Bill, 2025, passed by the Upper House of Parliament on 18 August 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indian Ports Act of 1908**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian Ports Bill, 2025**, was passed by the **Rajya Sabha** (Upper House of Parliament) on **18 August 2025**, marking a significant milestone in the modernization of India's maritime legal framework.
 
• This new legislation is designed to replace the **Indian Ports Act of 1908**, which had been the primary law regulating ports in India for over **117 years**.
 
• The primary objective of the **2025 Bill** is to repeal the archaic colonial-era **1908 Act** and provide a contemporary regulatory framework that addresses the current needs of the **maritime sector**, including safety, security, and administrative efficiency.
 
• The bill focuses on the holistic development of **non-major ports** (also known as minor ports) and ensures that their management is aligned with international maritime standards and **global best practices**.
 
• It empowers the **Maritime State Development Council (MSDC)** to act as an apex advisory body to ensure integrated planning and development of the entire **port sector** across the country's vast coastline.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Indian Ports Act, 1908:**
 
 
• Enacted during the **British colonial period**, this act provided for the administration of ports and the imposition of **port-dues**.
 
• It lacked comprehensive provisions for **environmental protection**, modern security protocols, and the structured development of **private sector participation** in port operations.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of the Indian Ports Bill, 2025:**
 
 
• **Safety and Security:** The bill incorporates the **International Ship and Port Facility Security (ISPS) Code**, ensuring that Indian ports meet global security requirements to prevent **maritime terrorism** and smuggling.
 
• **Pollution Control:** It introduces stringent measures for the **prevention of marine pollution**, mandating ports to have adequate facilities for the reception of **ship-generated waste** and oil residues.
 
• **Digitalization:** The legislation promotes the use of the **National Logistics Portal-Marine** to facilitate **Ease of Doing Business** by automating port clearances and documentation.
 
 
 
• **Classification of Ports in India:**
 
 
• **Major Ports:** Currently, India has **12 Major Ports** that are governed by the **Major Port Authorities Act, 2021**, and fall under the jurisdiction of the **Central Government**.
 
• **Non-Major Ports:** There are over **200 Non-Major Ports** distributed across the maritime states and Union Territories, which are generally managed by the **State Governments** or **Maritime Boards**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Maritime State Development Council (MSDC):** This council is a permanent body created to foster consultation between the **Union Government** and **State Governments**. It plays a critical role in preventing the duplication of port infrastructure and optimizing the use of **India's 7,517 km coastline**.
 
• **Economic Significance:** Approximately **95% by volume** and **70% by value** of India's external trade is handled through **maritime transport**, making the replacement of the **1908 Act** vital for achieving the target of a **5 trillion-dollar economy**.
 
• **Adjudication:** The **2025 Bill** provides for an **Adjudicatory Authority** to resolve disputes between ports and users, ensuring a transparent and time-bound grievance redressal mechanism.
</ul
